t: Guru Arjan built the shrine lower than its surroundings and open on all sides, so that worshippers walk down to it, and on 16 August 1604 he placed a copy of the Adi Granth in it.
Mughal and Afghan forces attacked the site repeatedly, most severely in 1762, when Ahmad Shah Durrani had it blown up with gunpowder, and the Sikhs returned each time to restore the pool and rebuild.

In June 1984 the Indian Army's Operation Blue Star against Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale and his followers in the complex damaged the shrine and destroyed the Akal Takht, and the casualty figures remain disputed.
dyk: Ranjit Singh's gilded copper panels for the roof were worth 500,000 rupees, and the first was placed on the shrine in 1803; the gold plating now includes a 400 kilogram dome and 750 kilograms of gold on the upper level.
ev: Guru Arjan began construction of the Harmandir Sahib, keeping the pool empty and dry while it was built
Guru Arjan placed a copy of the Adi Granth in the gurdwara and appointed Baba Buddha as the first granthi
Ahmad Shah Durrani had the Golden Temple blown up with gunpowder, and Jassa Singh Ahluwalia collected donations to rebuild it in 1764
Ranjit Singh donated gold to overlay the sanctum with gold leaf, after the renovation in marble and copper of 1809
Idols and images were removed from the Golden Temple after the campaign of the Tat Khalsa
The Indian Army carried out Operation Blue Star in the complex between 1 and 8 June, and the Akal Takht was destroyed
Sikhs rebuilt the Akal Takht Sahib, after repairs ordered in 1986 were removed

f.made: Begun by Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru, on a pool completed by Guru Ram Das; rebuilt by Sikhs after repeated destruction, and rebuilt in marble and copper by Maharaja Ranjit Singh, who overlaid the sanctum with gold leaf
f.form: A two-storey square sanctum, 12.25 by 12.25 metres, with a gold leaf dome, standing in a pool about 5.1 metres deep and reached by a causeway; a marble platform and a circumambulatory path 3.7 metres wide surround it, and four entrances open to the complex
f.where: Amritsar, Punjab, India, in a complex that includes the Akal Takht, the offices of the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, museums and a langar
f.known: the sanctum in the Amrit Sarovar pool; the gold plating on the dome and upper level; the four entrances open to all; the Guru Granth Sahib installed within; the langar, a free vegetarian kitchen; the Akal Takht, the chief seat of authority in Sikhism; Operation Blue Star in 1984
